questions.question: You need to optimize the performance of queries in BigQuery. Your tables are not partitioned or clustered. What optimization technique can you use?

questions.question: Your company recently migrated to Google Cloud and started using BigQuery. The team members don’t know how much querying they are going to do, and they need to be efficient with their spend. As a Professional Data Engineer, what pricing model would you recommend?

questions.question: Stella is a new member of a team in your company who has been put in charge of monitoring VM instances in the organization. Stella will need the required permissions to perform this role. How should you grant her those permissions?

questions.question: You need to add new groups of employees in Cymbal Superstore’s production environment. You need to consider Google’s recommendation of using least privilege. What should you do?

questions.question: Cymbal Superstore’s marketing department needs to load some slowly changing data into BigQuery. The data arrives hourly in a Cloud Storage bucket. You want to minimize cost and implement this in the fewest steps. What should you do?

questions.question: At Nimbus Outfitters you are planning storage for 25 TB of CSV files as part of a new analytics pipeline on Google Cloud. Teams across the company will run aggregate queries with different processing engines while the files remain in Cloud Storage. You want to keep the cost of running these aggregate queries as low as possible and still allow shared access across tools. Which storage approach and schema setup should you choose?
choices: Use Cloud Bigtable and run queries from an HBase shell on a Compute Engine VM
Store the data in Cloud Storage and create temporary external tables in BigQuery whenever users need to query
Keep the files in Cloud Storage and define permanent external tables in BigQuery that reference the CSV objects
Load the files into partitioned BigQuery managed tables and query directly in BigQuery
questions.explanation: Keep the files in Cloud Storage and define permanent external tables in BigQuery that reference the CSV objects. This approach lets all teams keep using the same CSV objects in Cloud Storage while BigQuery provides a shared schema and consistent SQL interface. With permanent external tables you avoid ingesting or duplicating 25 TB into BigQuery storage, which keeps storage spending down and preserves cross‑tool access to the files. You can manage schema centrally and control access with IAM, and queries are billed on the bytes BigQuery scans without extra data movement. Use Cloud Bigtable and run queries from an HBase shell on a Compute Engine VM is incorrect because Cloud Bigtable is designed for low latency operational workloads rather than ad hoc analytical aggregation on CSV files. It does not provide a SQL analytics layer for scanning large flat files and moving 25 TB into Bigtable would add complexity without meeting the requirement to keep files in Cloud Storage for shared use. Store the data in Cloud Storage and create temporary external tables in BigQuery whenever users need to query is incorrect because ad hoc temporary definitions add friction and inconsistency. The query cost is not lower than using a reusable definition and repeated setup hampers governance and reuse, whereas a permanent external definition provides a stable shared schema with less operational overhead. Load the files into partitioned BigQuery managed tables and query directly in BigQuery is incorrect because it moves the data into BigQuery storage which duplicates the 25 TB and prevents other tools from using the same Cloud Storage files. Although partitioning can reduce scanned bytes for some queries, it violates the requirement to keep the files in Cloud Storage and adds ongoing BigQuery storage cost. Cameron’s Google Cloud Certification Exam Tip When the requirement says the files must remain in Cloud Storage and be accessible to multiple tools, think BigQuery external tables. Prefer a permanent external table for shared schemas and consistent access rather than ad hoc temporary definitions.

questions.question: Is it possible to convert an existing single master Cloud Dataproc cluster to a high availability cluster with three masters using gcloud, and if so which command should you run?
choices: gcloud dataproc clusters repair my-ha-cluster –masters=3
You cannot change the master node count after the cluster is created
gcloud dataproc clusters update my-ha-cluster –num-masters=3
gcloud dataproc clusters create my-ha-cluster –num-masters=3
questions.explanation: You cannot change the master node count after the cluster is created. In Cloud Dataproc the number of master nodes is fixed at cluster creation time. If you need a high availability cluster with three masters you must create a new cluster with three masters and then move jobs or workflows to it. You cannot convert an existing single master cluster into a three master cluster using any gcloud operation. gcloud dataproc clusters repair my-ha-cluster –masters=3 is incorrect because the repair operation can replace failed instances or adjust workers but it does not support changing the number of master nodes, and the shown flag is not a supported way to add masters. gcloud dataproc clusters update my-ha-cluster –num-masters=3 is incorrect because the update command does not allow modifying the master count and there is no supported flag to change masters on an existing cluster. gcloud dataproc clusters create my-ha-cluster –num-masters=3 is incorrect for this question because it creates a new high availability cluster rather than converting an existing single master cluster. Cameron’s Google Cloud Certification Exam Tip When you see questions about changing core cluster topology, look for hints that the setting is immutable. If update or repair commands do not list a flag to change it, the safest answer is that you must recreate the resource with the desired configuration.

questions.question: Given 300 TB of training data accessed roughly every 30 days, with each job reading only a small subset, which Google Cloud Storage class provides low cost while remaining reliable and highly available?
choices: Cloud Storage Archive
Cloud Storage Nearline class
Cloud Storage Coldline storage
questions.explanation: Cloud Storage Nearline class. It provides low storage cost for data that is accessed about once per month while remaining highly durable and available. Cloud Storage Nearline class is optimized for infrequent access on the order of 30 days. The per gigabyte retrieval fees remain manageable when each training job reads only a small subset of the data and the 30 day minimum storage duration matches the usage pattern. It retains very high durability and offers strong availability across regional, dual region, or multi region locations. Cloud Storage Archive targets data that is rarely accessed such as once a year. It has a much longer minimum storage duration and higher retrieval costs and latency, which make it unsuitable and more expensive for data you touch every month. Cloud Storage Coldline storage is aimed at data accessed roughly once a quarter. It has a 90 day minimum storage duration and higher retrieval costs, so monthly access would typically incur more cost than Cloud Storage Nearline class and would not be the best fit compared to Nearline. Cameron’s Google Cloud Certification Exam Tip Match the storage class to access frequency. Use Nearline for about monthly access, Coldline for quarterly, and Archive for yearly, and always factor in retrieval charges and minimum storage durations when only a small subset is read.

questions.question: A fintech named OrionPay needs to orchestrate a multi stage analytics workflow that chains several Dataproc jobs and downstream Dataflow pipelines with strict task dependencies. The team wants a fully managed approach that provides retries, monitoring, and parameterized runs, and they must trigger it every weekday at 0315 UTC. Which Google Cloud service should they use to design and schedule this pipeline?
choices: Workflows
Cloud Composer
Cloud Scheduler
Dataproc Workflow Templates
questions.explanation: Cloud Composer because it is a fully managed Apache Airflow service that can orchestrate multi stage pipelines across Dataproc and Dataflow with strict task dependencies, includes retries and monitoring, supports parameterized runs, and can be scheduled to run every weekday at 0315 UTC. Airflow DAGs let you define ordered tasks that submit Dataproc jobs and then start Dataflow pipelines using native operators and sensors. You can configure per task retries and get centralized logging and monitoring in the service. You can pass parameters through DAG run configuration or templated fields and you can set a weekday cron schedule that runs at the required UTC time. Workflows can orchestrate API calls and supports retries and parameter passing, however it lacks the rich Airflow operators for Dataproc and Dataflow and it does not include native cron scheduling on its own, so you would need an extra scheduler and more custom logic to manage complex task dependencies. Cloud Scheduler only provides time based triggers for HTTP targets or Pub or Sub topics and it cannot model multi step dependencies or orchestrate Dataproc and Dataflow tasks with per task retries and detailed monitoring. Dataproc Workflow Templates can orchestrate sequences of Dataproc jobs with dependencies and parameters, however they do not natively include Dataflow steps and would still need an external scheduler for weekday runs, so they do not meet the cross service orchestration requirement. Cameron’s Google Cloud Certification Exam Tip Match the requirement to the orchestration level. If you need to chain Dataproc and Dataflow with strict dependencies and retries and monitoring then look for the managed Airflow option. Use Cloud Scheduler only for simple time based triggers and consider Dataproc Workflow Templates when all steps are Dataproc. Workflows fits API centric flows but usually pairs with a scheduler.

questions.question: You launched a Dataproc cluster to perform some Apache Spark jobs. You are looking for a method to securely transfer web traffic data between your machine’s web browser and Dataproc cluster.

VPN connection

These interfaces can be used to manage and monitor cluster resources and facilities, such as the YARN resource manager, the Hadoop Distributed File System (HDFS), MapReduce, and Spark. Other components or applications that you install on your cluster may also provide web interfaces. It is recommended to create an SSH tunnel for a secure connection between your web browser and Dataproc’s master node. SSH tunnel supports traffic proxying using the SOCKS protocol. To configure your browser to use the proxy, start a new browser session with proxy server parameters.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes the primary purpose of data governance in cloud data management?

To establish and enforce policies for managing data throughout its lifecycle
To optimize data storage and retrieval processes in cloud environments
To implement advanced encryption techniques for securing data in transit and at rest
questions.explanation: This is the most comprehensive and accurate description of data governance in cloud data management. It encompasses the overarching goal of data governance, which is to establish and maintain a framework for managing data throughout its entire lifecycle. This includes aspects of compliance, security, and optimization, but goes beyond these individual elements to create a holistic approach to data management.

questions.question: In the context of data management, what is the primary purpose of data cataloging?

To clean and transform raw data into a format suitable for analysis

questions.question: You are migrating on-premises data to a data warehouse on Google Cloud. This data will be made available to business analysts. Local regulations require that customer information including credit card numbers, phone numbers, and email IDs be captured, but not used in analysis. You need to use a reliable, recommended solution to redact the sensitive data. What should you do?
choices: Use Cloud DLP API to identify and redact data that matches infoTypes like credit card, phone, and email
Delete all columns with a title similar to credit card, phone, and email
Create a regular expression to identify and delete patterns that resemble credit card numbers, phone numbers, and email IDs
Use the Cloud DLP API to perform date shifting of any entries with credit card numbers, phone numbers, and email IDs
questions.explanation: DLP's built-in infoType detectors are purpose-built for this — reliable pattern detection plus redaction, without brittle manual regex or blind column deletion (which could remove needed columns entirely).

questions.question: You are running a user-supplied DoFn method signature pipeline in Dataflow. The function has been defined by you. The code is running slow and you want to further examine the pipeline code to get better visibility of why. What should you do?
choices: Use Cloud Monitoring
Use Cloud Logging
Use Cloud Profiler
Use Cloud Audit Logs

questions.question: Laws in the region where you operate require that files related to all orders made each day are stored immutably for 365 days. The solution that you recommend has to be cost-effective. What should you do?
choices: Store the data in a Cloud Storage bucket, and enable object versioning and delete any version older than 365 days
Store the data in a Cloud Storage bucket, and specify a retention period
Store the data in a Cloud Storage bucket, and set a lifecycle policy to delete the file after 365 days
Store the data in a Cloud Storage bucket, enable object versioning, and delete any version greater than 365
questions.explanation: A retention policy alone only prevents deletion — it doesn't clean up storage after day 365, costing more over time. A lifecycle rule automatically deletes files right at the 365-day mark, satisfying 'immutable for exactly 365 days' while staying cost-effective. Object versioning isn't needed since there's no mention of overwrites/edits.

questions.question: A company collects lots of consumer data from online marketing campaigns. Company plans to use Google Cloud to store this collected data. The top management is worried about exposing personally identifiable information (PII) that may be present in this data. What should you do to reduce the risk of exposing PII data?
choices: Use the Cloud Data Loss Prevention API (DLP API) to inspect and redact PII data.
Store all data in BigQuery and turn on column level access to protect sensitive data.
Ensure that all stored data is monitored by Security Command Center.
Ensure that all PII data is removed from the collected data before storing it on Google Cloud.
questions.explanation: Cloud DLP is purpose-built to inspect data for sensitive info types (like PII) and redact or mask it, making it the recommended tool over manual or ad hoc pattern matching.

questions.question: You have data that is ingested daily and frequently analyzed in the first month. Thereafter, the data is retained only for audits, which happen occasionally every few years. You need to configure cost-effective storage. What should you do?
choices: Create a bucket on Cloud Storage with object versioning configured
Create a bucket on Cloud Storage with Autoclass configured
Configure a data retention policy on Cloud Storage
Configure a lifecycle policy on Cloud Storage
questions.explanation: Autoclass automatically transitions objects between storage classes based on observed access patterns over time — exactly right when access frequency shifts from frequent to rare.

questions.question: A manager at Cymbal Retail expresses concern about unauthorized access to objects in your Cloud Storage bucket. You need to evaluate all access on all objects in the bucket. What should you do?
choices: Review the Admin Activity audit logs
Enable and then review the Data Access audit logs
Route the Admin Activity logs to a BigQuery sink and analyze the logs with SQL queries
Change the permissions on the bucket to only trusted employees
questions.explanation: Data Access audit logs capture reads/writes of the actual object data. Admin Activity logs only capture administrative/configuration changes to the bucket.

questions.question: Your data in BigQuery has some columns that are extremely sensitive. You need to enable only some users to see certain columns. What should you do?
choices: Create a new dataset with the column's data
Create a new table with the column's data
Use policy tags
Use IAM permissions
questions.explanation: Policy tags provide column-level security, restricting visibility of individual sensitive columns to specific users or groups. IAM operates at table/dataset level, not column level.

questions.question: You need to share inventory data from Cymbal Retail with a partner company that uses BigQuery to store and analyze its data. What tool can you use to securely and efficiently share the data?
choices: Analytics Hub
Cloud Data Loss Prevention (Cloud DLP)
Cloud Storage
Data Catalog
questions.explanation: Analytics Hub lets you securely publish curated BigQuery datasets that an external partner can subscribe to and query directly, without copying data or granting broad access.

questions.question: You have a Dataflow pipeline in production. For certain data, the system seems to be stuck longer than usual. This is causing delays in the pipeline execution. You want to reliably and proactively track and resolve such issues. What should you do?
choices: Review the Dataflow logs regularly
Set up alerts with Cloud Run functions code that reviews the audit logs regularly
Review the Cloud Monitoring dashboard regularly
Set up alerts on Cloud Monitoring based on system lag
questions.explanation: Proactive alerting on the system lag metric automatically notifies you of issues as they happen — reliable and proactive, unlike manually watching logs/dashboards.

questions.question: Cymbal Retail uses Google Cloud and has automated repeatable data processing workloads to achieve reliability and cost efficiency. You want out-of-the-box metric collection dashboards and the ability to generate alerts when specific conditions are met. What tool can you use?
choices: Cloud Monitoring
Data Catalog
Cloud Data Loss Prevention (Cloud DLP)
Cloud Composer
questions.explanation: Cloud Monitoring provides built-in dashboards and configurable alerting policies for metrics across Google Cloud services out of the box.

questions.question: Harborline Outfitters keeps tens of millions of records in a BigQuery date partitioned table named retail\\_ops.sales\\_events, and dashboards at example.com and internal services run aggregation queries dozens of times per minute. Each request calculates AVG, MAX and SUM across only the most recent 12 months of data, and the base table must preserve all historical rows for auditing. You want results that include brand new inserts while keeping compute cost, upkeep, and latency very low. What should you implement?
choices: Enable BigQuery BI Engine and query retail\\_ops.sales\\_events with a filter for the last 12 months of partitions
Create a scheduled query that rebuilds a 12 month aggregate summary table every 30 minutes
Create a materialized view that aggregates retail\\_ops.sales\\_events and restricts it to the last 12 months of partitions
Create a materialized view on retail\\_ops.sales\\_events and configure a partition expiration policy on the base table so only the last 12 months are kept
questions.explanation: Create a materialized view that aggregates retail\\_ops.sales\\_events and restricts it to the last 12 months of partitions. A materialized view precomputes AVG, MAX, and SUM and incrementally refreshes only the portions of data that change. This gives very low latency and cost for dashboards and services that run frequent aggregate queries. Restricting the materialized view to the most recent 12 months means queries scan far less data while the base table continues to hold all historical rows for auditing. BigQuery can also rewrite compatible queries to use the materialized view which reduces operational upkeep because clients do not need to change their SQL. Enable BigQuery BI Engine and query retail\\_ops.sales\\_events with a filter for the last 12 months of partitions is not the best fit because BI Engine is an in memory acceleration layer that does not precompute or incrementally maintain aggregates. You still pay for repeated scans or a large reservation and you do not get the same cost savings and simplicity that a preaggregated result provides. Create a scheduled query that rebuilds a 12 month aggregate summary table every 30 minutes is inefficient and increases maintenance. It introduces staleness between runs and repeatedly recomputes the entire window which drives cost and fails the requirement for near real time results. Create a materialized view on retail\\_ops.sales\\_events and configure a partition expiration policy on the base table so only the last 12 months are kept violates the requirement to preserve all historical rows for auditing because an expiration policy would delete older partitions from the base table. Cameron’s Google Cloud Certification Exam Tip When you see frequent aggregate queries that must stay fresh with low latency and cost, think materialized views. If the problem mentions an auditing need, avoid any option that expires or deletes base data.

questions.question: How should you design service account access to PII stored in Cloud Storage to enforce least privilege and enable auditability?
choices: One shared service account per project with CMEK on the buckets
Default Compute Engine service account with Project Editor for all workloads
Service accounts per workload with IAM groups and least privilege roles
Individual service accounts for each employee to access data
questions.explanation: Service accounts per workload with IAM groups and least privilege roles. The other options do not meet the requirements for least privilege and strong auditing. This approach assigns a unique identity to each workload which lets you grant only the minimum Cloud Storage roles that workload needs at the bucket or even prefix level. Because each workload uses its own service account, Cloud Audit Logs clearly attribute every access to a distinct principal which improves traceability for PII access and simplifies incident response. Managing permissions through groups streamlines administration at scale while still keeping fine grained bindings to specific buckets, prefixes, and keys. You can also pair this with CMEK by granting only the necessary Cloud KMS key roles to the same workload identities which keeps both data access and encryption permissions tightly scoped. This design reduces blast radius because revoking a single workload’s access is as simple as removing its service account from a group or role binding. It aligns with Google’s guidance to avoid basic roles and to use narrowly scoped predefined or custom roles for storage and key access which strengthens least privilege and auditability for sensitive data. One shared service account per project with CMEK on the buckets is incorrect because a shared identity prevents per workload attribution in audit logs and violates least privilege. CMEK improves encryption control but it does not fix the lack of identity separation when many services use the same account. Default Compute Engine service account with Project Editor for all workloads is incorrect because the default account is broadly shared and the Editor basic role is overly permissive. This combination undermines least privilege and makes it difficult to audit which workload accessed PII. Individual service accounts for each employee to access data is incorrect because service accounts are intended for non human workloads. Human access should use user identities and groups with strong controls and approvals and should not rely on per person service accounts for PII. Cameron’s Google Cloud Certification Exam Tip When a question mentions PII or auditability, choose designs that give each workload its own identity and grant only the needed roles on specific resources. Avoid basic roles and the default service account. Remember that CMEK complements but does not replace least privilege IAM.

questions.question: In Dataplex, how should you assign roles so engineers have full control of the sales lake and analysts have read-only access to curated data in the refined zone while maintaining governance within Dataplex?
choices: Grant the dataplex.dataReader role on the sales lake to engineering and grant the dataplex.dataOwner role on the refined zone to analytics
Assign dataplex.dataOwner on the sales lake to engineering and assign dataplex.dataReader on the refined zone to analytics
Grant BigQuery and Cloud Storage IAM roles directly on datasets and buckets for each group
Use Data Catalog policy tags and share BigQuery datasets without Dataplex roles
questions.explanation: Assign dataplex.dataOwner on the sales lake to engineering and assign dataplex.dataReader on the refined zone to analytics. Granting the dataOwner role on the lake to engineering centralizes data access through Dataplex and gives engineers comprehensive read and write access to the data in all assets attached to that lake. Granting the dataReader role on the refined zone to analytics limits analysts to read-only access on curated data in that specific zone. This follows the principle of least privilege and keeps governance in Dataplex because data roles applied at the lake or zone scope propagate to underlying BigQuery and Cloud Storage assets that are attached. This approach cleanly separates responsibilities. Engineers can fully work with data across the lake while analysts are constrained to curated datasets in the refined zone. It also avoids scattering IAM on individual datasets and buckets which preserves centralized governance and simpler audits. Grant the dataplex.dataReader role on the sales lake to engineering and grant the dataplex.dataOwner role on the refined zone to analytics is incorrect because it inverts the needed privileges. Engineers would be unable to make necessary changes in the lake and analysts would gain write capabilities in the refined zone which violates least privilege for curated data access. Grant BigQuery and Cloud Storage IAM roles directly on datasets and buckets for each group is incorrect because it bypasses Dataplex and fragments governance. The requirement is to keep governance in Dataplex which means you should grant data roles at the lake or zone level so access is centrally managed and consistently applied to attached assets. Use Data Catalog policy tags and share BigQuery datasets without Dataplex roles is incorrect because policy tags provide column level controls within BigQuery and do not manage access across all lake assets. This does not satisfy the need to keep governance in Dataplex or cover Cloud Storage assets that belong to the lake. Cameron’s Google Cloud Certification Exam Tip When a scenario says to keep governance in Dataplex prefer Dataplex data roles at the lake or zone. Map ownership or write needs to dataOwner and consumption to dataReader rather than granting IAM directly on datasets and buckets.

questions.question: Aurora Streams is moving its legacy warehouse to BigQuery and wants stronger collaboration across about 24 internal groups. The company needs a design that lets data producers securely publish curated read only datasets that others can easily discover and subscribe to without tickets. They also want subscribers to read the freshest data while keeping storage and operational costs low. Which approach should they use?
choices: Grant bigquery.dataViewer on each producer dataset to every subscribing team
Use BigQuery Data Transfer Service to replicate shared datasets into a central exchange project on an hourly schedule
Publish datasets through BigQuery Analytics Hub and let teams subscribe to linked datasets
Catalog producer datasets in Dataplex and control access with tag based IAM for consumer projects
questions.explanation: Publish datasets through BigQuery Analytics Hub and let teams subscribe to linked datasets. With Analytics Hub producers can publish curated read only datasets as listings that subscribers can easily discover and subscribe to. A subscription creates linked datasets in the consumer project that reference the publisher tables in place, which means queries always see the freshest data. Because linked datasets do not copy storage, costs remain low and producers operate a single authoritative dataset while sharing at scale without tickets. Grant bigquery.dataViewer on each producer dataset to every subscribing team is difficult to scale across about 24 groups and offers no discovery or subscription workflow. It increases administrative overhead and encourages ticket driven access management even though it can provide freshness. Use BigQuery Data Transfer Service to replicate shared datasets into a central exchange project on an hourly schedule duplicates data, raises storage cost, and introduces staleness between runs. The service is designed for scheduled transfers and copies rather than a publisher subscriber exchange model. Catalog producer datasets in Dataplex and control access with tag based IAM for consumer projects improves governance and discovery, yet it does not provide a subscription model with in place access. Tag based controls do not replace dataset level sharing in BigQuery, so teams would still need direct role management and would not get the simplicity and freshness of a linked dataset approach. Cameron’s Google Cloud Certification Exam Tip Map requirements for easy discovery, many consumers, read only sharing, freshest reads, and low storage to Analytics Hub with linked datasets. Options that copy data on a schedule usually mean higher cost and staler results.

questions.question: A company needs to process large volumes of data for business-critical processes while minimizing costs. They are considering using Dataproc for their data processing needs. What should they consider when deciding between persistent or job-based data clusters in Dataproc?
choices: Persistent clusters offer fixed capacity and are suitable for continuous, long-running processes, while job-based clusters are more cost-effective for short-lived, ad-hoc tasks.
Job-based clusters provide greater flexibility and cost efficiency for intermittent workloads, while persistent clusters are ideal for predictable, ongoing data processing tasks.
Persistent clusters are recommended for batch processing tasks due to their ability to scale resources dynamically, while job-based clusters are better suited for interactive query jobs.

Job-based clusters offer better fault tolerance and error recovery mechanisms, making them suitable for mission-critical data processes, while persistent clusters are more cost-effective for one-time data transformations.
questions.explanation: Option B is CORRECT as job-based clusters in Dataproc provide flexibility and cost efficiency for intermittent workloads by provisioning resources only when needed, while persistent clusters are better suited for predictable, ongoing data processing tasks where resources are continuously required. Option A is incorrect because persistent clusters may not be the most cost-effective option for short-lived, ad-hoc tasks due to their continuous resource allocation. Option C is incorrect because persistent clusters are not specifically recommended for batch processing tasks, and job-based clusters can also handle batch processing effectively. Option D is incorrect because fault tolerance and error recovery mechanisms are not distinguishing factors between persistent and job-based clusters in Dataproc. Both types of clusters offer fault tolerance capabilities. Reference Link: \u003chttps://cloud.google.com/dataproc/docs/concepts/compute/clusters-datalab-flex\u003e

questions.question: An organization wants to automate its data processing workflows using Cloud Composer. They need to schedule jobs in a repeatable manner to ensure the timely execution of critical tasks. What approach should they take to achieve this goal effectively?
choices: Utilize Cloud Functions to trigger workflows based on predefined schedules and dependencies.
Implement directed acyclic graphs (DAGs) in Cloud Composer to define workflow dependencies and schedule job execution.
Use Cloud Scheduler to define and manage job schedules, and then trigger workflow execution in Cloud Composer.
Leverage Cloud Tasks to create and manage task queues for scheduling and orchestrating data processing jobs in Cloud Composer.
questions.explanation: Option B is CORRECT as directed acyclic graphs (DAGs) in Cloud Composer allow organizations to define workflow dependencies and schedule job execution in a repeatable and reliable manner, ensuring timely execution of critical tasks. Option A is incorrect because while Cloud Functions can trigger workflows based on schedules and dependencies, they do not provide the same level of orchestration and scheduling capabilities as Cloud Composer DAGs. Option C is incorrect because Cloud Scheduler is primarily used for managing job schedules, but it does not offer workflow orchestration capabilities like Cloud Composer DAGs. Option D is incorrect because Cloud Tasks is more suitable for managing task queues and asynchronous task execution, rather than scheduling and orchestrating data processing workflows.

questions.question: Your organization needs to organize data workloads based on business requirements, considering factors like flexibility, capacity, and pricing models. Which pricing model offers fixed capacity and is best suited for predictable, steady workloads?
choices: Flex slot pricing
On-demand pricing
Flat-rate slot pricing
Pay-as-you-go pricing
questions.explanation: Option C is CORRECT as flat-rate slot pricing offers fixed capacity for predictable workloads. It allows users to pay a flat rate for a set number of slots, regardless of usage, providing stability in pricing for steady workloads. Option A is incorrect because flex slot pricing offers flexibility and dynamically allocates slots based on demand, making it suitable for fluctuating workloads. Option B is incorrect because on-demand pricing charges users based on usage, without any fixed commitments, making it suitable for sporadic or unpredictable workloads. Option D is incorrect because pay-as-you-go pricing is similar to on-demand pricing and charges users based on actual usage, without fixed commitments.

questions.question: Your organization needs to ensure the observability of data processes, monitor planned usage, and troubleshoot error messages and billing issues effectively. Which Google Cloud service provides centralized logging and monitoring capabilities for data processes?
choices: Google Cloud Monitoring
Google Cloud Logging
Google Cloud Trace
Google Cloud Audit Logging
questions.explanation: Option A is CORRECT as Google Cloud Monitoring provides centralized logging and monitoring capabilities for Google Cloud services, including data processes such as Dataproc and Dataflow. It enables users to collect, view, and analyze metrics, logs, and other monitoring data across their Google Cloud environment. Option B is incorrect because while Google Cloud Logging offers centralized logging capabilities, it does not provide comprehensive monitoring functionalities for data processes such as planned usage monitoring and error troubleshooting. Option C is incorrect because Google Cloud Trace is primarily focused on distributed application tracing, providing insights into application performance, rather than centralized logging and monitoring for data processes. Option D is incorrect because Google Cloud Audit Logging is specifically designed for tracking and logging user access and system activity within Google Cloud Platform services, not for monitoring data processes.

questions.question: Your organization operates critical data processes in a Google Cloud environment. You need to decide between persistent or job-based data clusters for processing large-scale data workloads efficiently. What should you consider when making this decision?
choices: Evaluate the cost-effectiveness of persistent clusters based on long-term utilization trends.
Implement job-based clusters to ensure scalability and resource optimization for irregular workloads.
Analyze the availability of resources in persistent clusters to ensure uninterrupted data processing.
Use persistent clusters to avoid the overhead of cluster initialization and termination.
questions.explanation: Option B is CORRECT as implementing job-based clusters allows for scalability and resource optimization, especially for irregular workloads, ensuring efficient utilization of resources without incurring unnecessary costs. Option A is incorrect because while evaluating the cost-effectiveness of persistent clusters is important, it may not address the scalability and optimization needs for sporadic workloads. Option C is incorrect because analyzing resource availability in persistent clusters may ensure uninterrupted processing but may not offer the flexibility needed for varying workloads. Option D is incorrect because opting for persistent clusters to avoid initialization and termination overhead may lead to underutilization of resources and increased costs for sporadic workloads.

questions.question: You are using Dataproc to process a large number of CSV files. The storage option you choose needs to be flexible to serve many worker nodes in multiple clusters. These worker nodes will read the data and also write to it for intermediate storage between processing jobs. What is the recommended storage option on Google Cloud?
choices: Cloud SQL
Zonal persistent disks
Local SSD
Cloud Storage
questions.explanation: Cloud Storage is decoupled from any single node, zone, or cluster, and is accessible to all worker nodes across multiple clusters simultaneously — persistent disks and local SSD are bound to a specific node/zone.

questions.question: Cymbal Retail has accumulated a large amount of data. Analysts and leadership are finding it difficult to understand the meaning of the data, such as BigQuery columns. Users of the data don't know who owns what. You need to improve the searchability of the data. What should you do?
choices: Create tags for data entries in Cloud Data Catalog
Rename BigQuery columns with more descriptive names
Export the data to Cloud Storage with descriptive file names
Add a description column corresponding to each data column
questions.explanation: Data Catalog is the centralized metadata management and tagging tool built specifically to improve discoverability, clarify ownership, and make datasets searchable.

questions.question: [Bonus Quiz] A Dataflow pipeline at Cymbal Superstore must process transactions, writing valid records to BigQuery and records with a null transaction_id to a dead-letter location in Cloud Storage. What is the most efficient, idiomatic Dataflow pattern to achieve this?
choices: Run the pipeline twice: once to filter for valid records and a second time to filter for invalid records
Use a ParDo transform with a main output for valid records and a tagged side output for invalid records
Write all data to a temporary BigQuery table and then use a SQL query to split the data
Use a GroupByKey transform to group records by whether the transaction_id is null or not
questions.explanation: A ParDo with a tagged side output is the standard, single-pass pattern in Dataflow for splitting one data stream based on validation logic.

questions.question: You have a team of data analysts that run queries interactively on BigQuery during work hours. You also have thousands of report generation queries that run simultaneously. You often see: Exceeded rate limits: too many concurrent queries for this project_and_region. How would you resolve this issue?
choices: Run all queries in interactive mode
Create a yearly reservation of BigQuery slots
Run the report generation queries in batch mode
Create a view to run the queries
questions.explanation: Offloading the report generation queries to batch mode reduces the number of concurrent interactive queries hitting the concurrency limit.

questions.question: One of your encryption keys stored in Cloud KMS was exposed. You need to re-encrypt all of your CMEK-protected Cloud Storage data that used that key, and then delete the compromised key. You also want to reduce the risk of objects getting written without CMEK protection in the future. What should you do?
choices: Rotate the Cloud KMS key version. Continue to use the same Cloud Storage bucket.
Create a new Cloud KMS key. Set the default CMEK key on the existing Cloud Storage bucket to the new one.
Create a new Cloud KMS key. Create a new Cloud Storage bucket. Copy all objects from the old bucket to the new bucket while specifying the new Cloud KMS key in the copy command.
Create a new Cloud KMS key. Create a new Cloud Storage bucket configured to use the new key as the default CMEK key. Copy all objects from the old bucket to the new bucket without specifying a key.
questions.explanation: A new bucket with CMEK as its default ensures any data subsequently written to it — including the existing data being copied over — is automatically protected with the new key. Rotating the key version doesn't re-encrypt existing data; setting a new default on the existing bucket only protects future writes; copying with the key specified works for re-encryption but doesn't set a bucket default, so future writes could still land without CMEK.

questions.question: You need to connect multiple applications with dynamic public IP addresses to a Cloud SQL instance. You configured users with strong passwords and enforced SSL. You want to use Cloud SQL public IP and ensure secured connections. What should you do?
choices: Add all application networks to Authorized Network and regularly update them.
Add CIDR 0.0.0.0/0 to Authorized Network. Use IAM to add users.
Add CIDR 0.0.0.0/0 to Authorized Network. Use Cloud SQL Auth proxy on all applications.
Leave the Authorized Network empty. Use Cloud SQL Auth proxy on all applications.
questions.explanation: Cloud SQL Auth proxy secures connections for applications with dynamically assigned IPs, without needing to whitelist any network. Opening 0.0.0.0/0 exposes the instance to the entire public internet, and manually updating IP entries can't keep up with dynamic IPs.

questions.question: You are preparing an organization-wide dataset. You need to preprocess customer data stored in a restricted bucket in Cloud Storage. The data will be used to create consumer analyses. You need to comply with data privacy requirements. What should you do?
choices: Use Dataflow and Cloud KMS to encrypt sensitive fields and write the encrypted data in BigQuery. Share the encryption key by following the principle of least privilege.
Use the Cloud DLP API and Dataflow to detect and remove sensitive fields from the data in Cloud Storage. Write the filtered data in BigQuery.
Use Dataflow and the Cloud DLP API to mask sensitive data. Write the processed data in BigQuery.
Use CMEK to directly encrypt the data in Cloud Storage. Use federated queries from BigQuery. Share the encryption key by following the principle of least privilege.
questions.explanation: Masking with DLP + Dataflow satisfies data privacy compliance while preserving the overall data for analysis. Removing sensitive fields entirely is scalable but discards data that could enrich the analysis; encrypting fields/bucket-wide isn't a scalable pattern for an org-wide dataset.

questions.question: Your organization has two Google Cloud projects, project A and project B. In project A, you have a Pub/Sub topic that receives data from confidential sources. Only resources in project A should access the data in that topic, and no other current or future project should be able to. What should you do?
choices: Configure VPC Service Controls in the organization with a perimeter around project A.
Configure VPC Service Controls in the organization with a perimeter around the VPC of project A.
Add firewall rules in project A so only traffic from the VPC in project A is permitted.
Use IAM conditions to ensure that only users and service accounts in project A can access resources in project A.
questions.explanation: The core problem is data exfiltration out of project A — exactly what VPC-SC perimeters are for, and Pub/Sub is a VPC-SC supported product. A VPC-only perimeter or firewall rules have no effect on Pub/Sub since it's serverless; IAM conditions aren't supported on Pub/Sub.

questions.question: You are on the data governance team and are implementing security requirements. You need to encrypt all your data in BigQuery using an encryption key managed by your team. You must generate and store encryption material only on your on-premises HSM. You want to rely on Google managed solutions. What should you do?
choices: Create the key in the on-prem HSM, and import it into a Cloud KMS key. Associate the Cloud KMS key while creating BigQuery resources.
Create the key in the on-prem HSM, and import it into a Cloud HSM key. Associate the Cloud HSM key while creating BigQuery resources.
Create the key in the on-prem HSM and link it to a Cloud EKM key. Associate the Cloud EKM key while creating BigQuery resources.
Create the key in the on-prem HSM. Create BigQuery resources and encrypt data while ingesting them into BigQuery.
questions.explanation: Cloud EKM is the only option that lets the key material stay generated and stored exclusively on the external (on-prem) HSM while remaining a Google-managed integration usable by BigQuery. KMS and Cloud HSM both require exporting/importing the key, so it no longer lives only on-prem.

questions.question: You have an upstream process that writes data to Cloud Storage, read by a Spark job on Dataproc in us-central1, but data could be stored anywhere in the US. You need recovery for a catastrophic single region failure with RPO=15 mins, and minimal latency when reading data. What should you do?
choices: Create a US multi-region bucket. Run Dataproc in us-central1 reading from it. On failure, redeploy Dataproc to us-central2, keep reading from same bucket.

Create a dual-region bucket (us-central1 & us-south1) with turbo replication. Run Dataproc in us-central1 reading from the same-region bucket. On failure, redeploy Dataproc to us-south1, read from the same bucket.
Create two regional buckets (us-central1, us-south1). Write to us-central1; use Storage Transfer Service hourly to copy to us-south1. Run Dataproc in us-central1. On failure, redeploy to us-south1.

Create a dual-region bucket (us-central1 & us-south1) with turbo replication. Run Dataproc in us-central1 reading from the us-south1 bucket. On failure, redeploy to us-south1, continue reading from same bucket.
questions.explanation: Dual-region buckets with turbo replication guarantee a 15-minute RPO, and keeping the Dataproc cluster colocated with the bucket's primary region minimizes read latency. Multi-region buckets have ~1-hour RPO; hourly STS copies can't meet 15-min RPO; reading cross-region before any failure needlessly adds latency.

questions.question: You maintain ETL pipelines. A streaming Dataflow pipeline is taking a long time to process incoming data, causing output delays, and the pipeline graph was automatically optimized and merged into one step. You want to identify where the bottleneck is occurring. What should you do?
choices: Insert output sinks after each key processing step, and observe the writing throughput of each block.
Log debug information in each ParDo function, and analyze the logs at execution time.
Insert a Reshuffle operation after each processing step, and monitor the execution details in the Dataflow console.
Verify that the Dataflow service accounts have appropriate permissions to write the processed data to the output sinks.
questions.explanation: Inserting a Reshuffle after each step prevents Dataflow's automatic fusion of steps, letting you observe each step's throughput separately in the console — directly revealing the bottleneck.

questions.question: You need to modernize your on-premises data strategy: Hadoop clusters with HDFS, and Airflow orchestrating hundreds of ETL pipelines with thousands of steps. You need a new GCP architecture requiring minimal changes to existing orchestration. What should you do?
choices: Use Dataproc for Hadoop, Cloud Storage for HDFS. Convert ETL pipelines to Dataflow.
Use Dataproc for Hadoop, Cloud Storage for HDFS. Orchestrate pipelines with Cloud Composer.
Use Bigtable for large workloads, connect to Cloud Storage for HDFS. Orchestrate with Cloud Composer.
Use Dataproc for Hadoop, Cloud Storage for HDFS. Use Cloud Data Fusion to visually design and deploy ETL pipelines.
questions.explanation: Dataproc + Cloud Storage is the direct lift-and-shift path for Hadoop/HDFS, and Cloud Composer (managed Airflow) requires minimal changes since it's the same orchestration engine already in use.

questions.question: You are designing a Cloud Storage architecture with pipelines reading raw data from one bucket and writing processed data to a second bucket. You want resilience to regional failure, minimized RPO, with no impact on applications. What should you do?
choices: Adopt multi-regional Cloud Storage buckets.
Adopt two regional buckets, and update your application to write output to both.
Adopt a dual-region bucket, and enable turbo replication.
Adopt two regional buckets, and create a daily task to copy from one to the other.
questions.explanation: A dual-region bucket with turbo replication guarantees a 15-minute RPO with zero required application changes. Writing to two buckets requires app changes; a daily copy task has up to 24-hour RPO.

questions.question: You are building an ELT solution in BigQuery using Dataform. You need to perform uniqueness and null value checks on your final tables. What should you do to efficiently integrate these checks into your pipeline?
choices: Build Dataform assertions into your code.
Create Dataplex data quality tasks.
Build BigQuery user-defined functions (UDFs).
Write a Spark-based stored procedure.
questions.explanation: Dataform assertions are built specifically to run data quality checks as an integrated part of a Dataform job/pipeline. Dataplex tasks live outside the pipeline; UDFs and Spark procedures aren't typical tools for this.

questions.question: [Choose two] You recently deployed several data processing jobs into your Cloud Composer 2 environment. Some tasks fail, and monitoring shows increased total workers memory usage and worker pod evictions. What should you do?
choices: Increase the DAG file parsing interval.
Increase the Cloud Composer 2 environment size from medium to large.
Increase the memory available to the Airflow workers.
Increase the memory available to the Airflow triggerer.
Increase the maximum number of workers and reduce worker concurrency.
questions.explanation: Worker pod evictions with rising worker memory usage point to an out-of-memory situation on the workers. Increasing worker memory directly relieves that pressure, and increasing max workers while lowering per-worker concurrency spreads tasks out, further reducing memory pressure per worker.

questions.question: Your business users need to clean and prepare data before analysis, prefer GUIs for transformations, and then want to analyze the transformed data directly in a spreadsheet. What should you do?
choices: Use Dataprep to clean the data, and write the results to BigQuery. Analyze the data using Connected Sheets.
Use Dataprep to clean the data, and write the results to BigQuery. Analyze the data using Looker Studio.
Use Dataflow to clean the data, and write the results to BigQuery. Analyze the data using Connected Sheets.
Use Dataflow to clean the data, and write the results to BigQuery. Analyze the data using Looker Studio.
questions.explanation: Two requirements must both be met: a GUI-based cleaning tool (Dataprep, not Dataflow) and a spreadsheet-based analysis tool (Connected Sheets, not the dashboard tool Looker Studio).

questions.question: You are designing a Dataflow pipeline for a batch processing job. You want to mitigate multiple zonal failures at job submission time. What should you do?
choices: Specify a worker region by using the --region flag.
Create an Eventarc trigger to resubmit the job in case of zonal failure when submitting the job.
Submit duplicate pipelines in two different zones by using the --zone flag.
Set the pipeline staging location as a regional Cloud Storage bucket.
questions.explanation: Specifying a region (instead of pinning to one zone) lets Dataflow automatically pick the best available zone at submission time, adding built-in fault tolerance against zonal failure.

questions.question: Different teams store customer and performance data in BigQuery. Each team needs full control of their data, ability to query within their projects, and ability to exchange data with other teams. You need an org-wide solution minimizing operational tasks and costs. What should you do?
choices: Ask each team to create authorized views of their data. Grant the bigquery.jobUser role to each team.
Ask each team to publish their data in BigQuery sharing (Analytics Hub). Direct other teams to subscribe to them.
Create a BigQuery scheduled query to replicate all customer data into team projects.
Enable each team to create materialized views of the data they need to access in their projects.
questions.explanation: Analytics Hub automatically creates an authorized, linked dataset the moment another team subscribes — no manual per-team authorization management, and no data duplication like the other options.

questions.question: Your healthcare organization has data organized and managed by respective data owners across various storage services, making discovery and management difficult. You need a cost-optimized solution for data management/discovery, lineage tracking, and data quality validation. How should you build the solution?
choices: Build a new data discovery tool on GKE for source onboarding and lineage tracking.
Use BigLake to convert the current solution into a data lake architecture.
Use Dataplex to manage data, track data lineage, and perform data quality validation.
Use BigQuery to track data lineage, and use Dataprep to manage data and perform data quality validation.
questions.explanation: Dataplex is purpose-built to manage decentralized data across multiple storage systems, track lineage, and run data quality validation — all without migrating anything.

questions.question: You want to store your team's shared tables in a single dataset, readable but unmodifiable by analysts, while giving each analyst an individual workspace in the same project for their own tables, inaccessible to other analysts. What should you do?
choices: Give analysts BigQuery Data Viewer at the project level. Create one other dataset, give analysts Data Editor on that dataset.
Give analysts BigQuery Data Viewer at the project level. Create a dataset per analyst, give each Data Editor at the project level.
Give analysts BigQuery Data Viewer on the shared dataset. Create a dataset per analyst, give each Data Editor at the dataset level for their own dataset.
Give analysts BigQuery Data Viewer on the shared dataset. Create one other dataset, give analysts Data Editor on that dataset.
questions.explanation: Three conditions must all hold: Viewer scoped to the shared dataset only (not project-wide), one separate dataset per analyst for real isolation, and Editor scoped to each analyst's own dataset specifically.

questions.question: You have several different file type data sources (Parquet, CSV). You want to store the data in Cloud Storage with an object sink that allows using your own encryption keys, and you want a GUI-based solution. What should you do?
choices: Use Storage Transfer Service to move files into Cloud Storage.
Use Dataflow to move files into Cloud Storage.
Use Cloud Data Fusion to move files into Cloud Storage.
Use BigQuery Data Transfer Service to move files into BigQuery.
questions.explanation: Cloud Data Fusion has connectors supporting customer-managed encryption keys and offers a fully GUI-based, code-free experience for moving files into Cloud Storage. STS doesn't support CMEK; Dataflow requires code; BigQuery Data Transfer Service targets BigQuery, not Cloud Storage.

questions.question: You are designing a real-time ride-hailing demand system ingesting via Pub/Sub, aggregating supply/demand data for the last 30 seconds every 2 seconds, storing results in a low-latency system for real-time dashboards. What should you do?
choices: Group data using a tumbling window in Dataflow, write aggregated data to Memorystore.
Group data using a hopping window in Dataflow, write aggregated data to Memorystore.
Group data using a session window in Dataflow, write aggregated data to BigQuery.
Group data using a hopping window in Dataflow, write aggregated data to BigQuery.
questions.explanation: A hopping window naturally computes 'last 30 seconds, every 2 seconds' via overlapping sliding windows. Memorystore gives the low-latency access real-time dashboards need; BigQuery is not built for this latency requirement.

questions.question: You have terabytes of customer behavioral data streaming into BigQuery daily, plus customer preferences in Cloud SQL (MySQL) and CRM on Cloud SQL (PostgreSQL). Marketing wants to combine all three for campaigns run 100-300 times/day, while keeping load on Cloud SQL minimal. What should you do?
choices: Create BigQuery connections to both Cloud SQL databases. Use federated queries on the databases and Google Analytics data.
Create a Dataproc cluster with Trino to connect to both Cloud SQL databases and BigQuery.
Create streams in Datastream to replicate the required tables from both Cloud SQL databases to BigQuery.
Create a job on Apache Spark with Dataproc Serverless to query both Cloud SQL databases and BigQuery.
questions.explanation: Datastream replicates the needed tables into BigQuery via CDC, so hundreds of daily campaign queries run entirely against BigQuery, keeping load on Cloud SQL minimal. Federated queries and Trino/Spark options all pull heavy load onto the live databases or repeatedly out of BigQuery.

questions.question: You have an Oracle database in a VM in a VPC network. You want to replicate and continuously synchronize 50 tables to BigQuery while minimizing infrastructure management. What should you do?
choices: Deploy Apache Kafka in the same VPC, use Kafka Connect Oracle CDC, and the Kafka Connect BigQuery Sink Connector.
Deploy Apache Kafka in the same VPC, use Kafka Connect Oracle CDC, and Dataflow to stream the Kafka topic to BigQuery.
Create a Datastream service from Oracle to BigQuery, use private connectivity to the same VPC, and a connection profile to BigQuery.
Create a Pub/Sub subscription to write to BigQuery directly. Deploy the Debezium Oracle connector to capture changes, sink to the Pub/Sub topic.
questions.explanation: Datastream is a fully serverless CDC service — no infrastructure to manage. Both Kafka-based options and the Debezium option all require deploying and managing a VM-based service.

questions.question: You are using Workflows to call an API returning a 1KB JSON response, apply complex business logic (using Python's standard library, beyond what Workflows offers), then load a Cloud Storage file to BigQuery. You want simplicity and speed of execution. What should you do?
choices: Create a Dataproc cluster, and use PySpark to apply the logic on your JSON file.
Invoke a Cloud Run function instance that uses Python to apply the logic on your JSON file.
Invoke a subworkflow in Workflows to apply the logic on your JSON file.
Create a Cloud Composer environment and run the logic in Cloud Composer.
questions.explanation: A Cloud Run function spins up quickly and natively supports Python — matching the 'simplicity and speed' goal for a tiny 1KB payload. Dataproc and Composer are massive overkill; a Workflows subworkflow still lacks Python's standard library.

questions.question: You need to look at BigQuery data from a specific table multiple times a day. The underlying table is several petabytes, but you want to filter and provide simple aggregations to downstream users, running queries faster with up-to-date insights. What should you do?
choices: Run a scheduled query to pull the necessary data at specific intervals daily.
Use a cached query to accelerate time to results.
Limit the query columns being pulled in the final result.
Create a materialized view based off of the query being run.
questions.explanation: Materialized views pre-aggregate/pre-filter data, dramatically speeding up repeated queries on a PB-scale table, and auto-refresh incrementally as source data changes — keeping insights fresh without manual scheduling.

questions.question: You administer a BigQuery on-demand environment. Your BI tool submits hundreds of daily queries aggregating a 50 TB sales history table at day/month levels, which are slow and over cost expectations. You need faster response, lower cost, and minimal maintenance. What should you do?
choices: Build materialized views on top of the sales table to aggregate data at the day and month level.
Build authorized views on top of the sales table to aggregate data at the day and month level.
Enable BI Engine and add your sales table as a preferred table.
Create a scheduled query to build sales day and sales month aggregate tables on an hourly basis.
questions.explanation: Materialized views pre-aggregate the data so each query scans far less, with low maintenance since BigQuery keeps them refreshed automatically. Authorized views don't improve performance; BI Engine can't cache a full 50TB table; scheduled queries require active maintenance.

questions.question: You designed a BigQuery data warehouse for sales data. You want a self-serving, low-maintenance, cost-effective way to share the sales dataset with other business units. What should you do?
choices: Use BigQuery Data Transfer Service to schedule copies of the sales dataset to other business units' projects.
Create and share views with the users in the other business units.
Create a BigQuery sharing (Analytics Hub) private exchange, and publish the sales dataset.
Enable the other business units' projects to access the authorized views of the sales dataset.
questions.explanation: Analytics Hub is cost-effective (no data copies) and low-maintenance (other units self-serve subscription, no data-producer involvement needed). Scheduled copies increase storage cost and staleness; authorized views require ongoing reauthorization maintenance.

questions.question: You orchestrate ETL pipelines using Cloud Composer. One task in the Airflow DAG relies on a third-party service. You want to be notified when the task does not succeed. What should you do?
choices: Assign a function with notification logic to the on_failure_callback parameter for the operator.
Assign a function with notification logic to the sla_miss_callback parameter for the operator.
Assign a function with notification logic to the on_retry_callback parameter for the operator.
Configure a Cloud Monitoring alert on the sla_missed metric associated with the task.
questions.explanation: on_failure_callback fires specifically when the task fails — the exact event needed. sla_miss_callback fires on SLA breach (time-based), on_retry_callback fires only during retries, and the Monitoring alert watches the wrong metric.

questions.question: You need to create a SQL pipeline that runs an aggregate SQL transformation on a BigQuery table every two hours and appends the result to another table. It must retry on errors, and send an email after three consecutive failures. What should you do?
choices: Create a BigQuery scheduled query with a two-hour repeat schedule, and enable email notifications.
Use the BigQueryUpsertTableOperator in Cloud Composer, set retry to three, and email_on_failure to true.
Create a BigQuery scheduled query with a two-hour repeat schedule and Pub/Sub notification; use Pub/Sub and Cloud Run functions to send email after three failures.
Use the BigQueryInsertJobOperator in Cloud Composer, set retry to three, and email_on_failure to true.
questions.explanation: BigQueryInsertJobOperator can run the SQL transformation and append results, and with retry=3 plus email_on_failure=True it retries up to three times before emailing on final failure. BigQuery scheduled queries have no built-in retry option at all, and BigQueryUpsertTableOperator is for table property changes, not SQL transformations.

questions.question: You want to launch a Cloud Machine Learning Engine cluster to deploy a deep neural network model built by Tensorflow by data scientists of your company. Reviewing the standard tiers available by Google ML Engine, you could not find a tier that suits the requirements data scientists need for the cluster. Google allows you to specify custom cluster specification.
choices: workerCount
parameterServerCount
masterCount
workerMemory
questions.explanation: The Custom tier is not a set tier, but rather enables you to use your own cluster specification. When you use this tier, set values to configure your processing cluster according to these guidelines: - You must set TrainingInput.masterType to specify the type of machine to use for your master node. This is the only required setting. See the machine types described below.   - You may set TrainingInput.workerCount to specify the number of workers to use. If you specify one or more workers, you must also set TrainingInput.workerType to specify the type of machine to use for your worker nodes.   - You may set TrainingInput.parameterServerCount to specify the number of parameter servers to use. If you specify one or more parameter servers, you must also set TrainingInput.parameterServerType to specify the type of machine to use for your parameter servers. From the explanation, specifications can be set from the answers are workerCount & parameterServerCount.

questions.question: You are building a model using TensorFlow. Upon training the model, the results show that the model could return 73% true positives. When you tested the model with a set derived from real data. You noticed a decrease in true positive returns to 65%. You need to tune the model for better prediction. What would you do?
choices: Increase feature parameters
Increase regularization
Decrease feature parameters
Decrease regularization
questions.explanation: Overfitting happens when a model performs well on a training set, generating only a small error while giving wrong output for the test set. This happens because the model is only picking up specific features input found in the training set instead of picking out the general features of the given training set. To solve overfitting, the following would help in improving the model’s quality: - Increase the number of examples, the more data a model is trained with, the more use cases the model can be training on and better improves its predictions.   - Tune hyperparameters which are related to number and size of hidden layers (for neural networks), and regularization, which means using techniques to make your model simpler such as using dropout method to remove neuron networks or adding “penalty” parameters to the cost function.   - Remove features by removing irrelevant features. Feature engineering is a wide subject and feature selection is a critical part of building and training a model. Some algorithms have built-in feature selection, but in some cases, data scientists need to cherry-pick or manually select or remove features for debugging and finding the best model output. From the brief explanation, to solve the overfitting problem in the scenario, you need to:   - Increase the training set.   - Decrease features parameters.   - Increase regularization.

questions.question: You are building a machine learning model using TensorFlow. The model aims to predict the next earthquake’s locations, approximate time and Richter scale based on data records since 1913. The model needs tuning each number of epochs on training data for higher accuracy. Which of the variables are used for hyperparameter tuning?
choices: Number of features
Number of hidden layers
Number of nodes in hidden layers
Weight values
questions.explanation: Hyperparameters are the variables that govern the training process itself. For example, part of setting up a deep neural network is deciding how many hidden layers of nodes to use between the input layer and the output layer, and how many nodes each layer should use. These variables are not directly related to the training data but these are configuration variables. Note that parameters change during a training job, while hyperparameters are usually constant during a job. Option A is incorrect: Numbers of features is set by feature engineering, not hyperparameter tuning.   Option D is incorrect: Weight values are set while training the model.

questions.question: Choose all statement(s) which is/are correct for cloud pub/sub.
choices: Cloud PubSub has default retention period of 7 days.
The retention period for cloud pubsub is configurable and can be configured to a maximum of 28 days and a minimum of 10 minutes.
The retention period for cloud pubsub is configurable and can be configured to a maximum of 7 days and a minimum of 10 minutes.
Retention period for cloud pub/sub is not configurable and is set to 7 days by default.
questions.explanation: Option A is correct. Cloud pub/sub has default retention period of 7 days.   Option B is incorrect. Cloud pub/sub retention period is configurable and can be configured to a maximum of 7 days and a minimum of 10 minutes.   Option C is correct. Cloud pub/sub retention period is configurable and can be configured to a maximum of 7 days and a minimum of 10 minutes   Option D is incorrect. Cloud pub/sub retention period is configurable.
